data.name: HelpCanISeeQ
data.value: Can I see Today in my calendar?
data.comment: Question on the Help page. Today is the name of the Today page.

data.name: HelpCanISeeA1
data.value: Yes. Under Today in your calendar in Settings you get a private link to add to your calendar app: Add to Google Calendar, or Other calendar apps on iPhone, Mac and Outlook. You can also copy the link and add it by its address (From URL in Google Calendar on a computer, Add subscribed calendar on iPhone). Each day with something due gets one all-day event with what Today will ask, for the next 30 days, and it never says to water. Under the link you can pick what shows, for example leave out the photo round. It needs an account and works without notifications.
data.comment: Answer on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: HelpCanISeeA2
data.value: Calendar apps fetch the link on their own schedule, from every hour to about once a day for Google, so something you just did can show for a while. Changes go up the next time the app syncs.
data.comment: Second paragraph of the answer.

data.name: HelpWhoQ
data.value: Who can see my calendar link?
data.comment: Question on the Help page.

data.name: HelpWhoA1
data.value: Anyone who has the link can see what's due and your plants' names, so keep it to your calendar apps. Stikling only keeps a fingerprint of it, so only the device that made it can show it again. Make a new link or Turn off stops the old one straight away. Events already in a calendar stay until it fetches again.
data.comment: Answer on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.
